classes.legitimate-data-label: Content, a label, or recorded provenance. Belongs in the game and cannot become one world's fixed gameplay instance.
classes.dev-or-test-only-fixture: A fixture literal a test, a developer route or explicit scenario data may hold, and that ordinary New Game and Continue cannot reach.
classes.production-hardcode: A world-instance gameplay identity an ordinary player can be handed because a production module spells it out. None may remain.

note: Every case is listed by its exact literal. There are no file-wide wildcards: a new world-instance literal in a file already listed here is unclassified and fails the census, exactly as one in a new file would.

trackedExceptions.note: Not census cases — no world-instance literal is involved — but the surfaces this role is still working through. Listed so a reviewer sees them next to the clean census rather than instead of it.

kentuckyPinnedSitting.status: The one authored deliberation sitting. Its measure identity is now the world's — the sections, the fiscal note, the amounts and the beneficiary are bound to the bill actually on file, and the room fails closed when they would describe a different bill. The sitting's own cast and place are still written for Kentucky; a second authored sitting, not a deletion, is what widens it.

fixtureNamedModulesOnPlayGraph.note: Each is now individually classified rather than pinned as a group. `src/presentation/run-a-fixture.ts` was on this list and is no longer on the ordinary-play graph at all: the dossier stopped naming places through its helper.

src/environment/scenes/committee-room-fi.finding: A registered room. Scene geometry and backdrop, not a gameplay instance; it names no measure, person or outcome. Renderer scope belongs to ROLE D.

src/simulation/demo-jurisdiction-context.finding: DEMO_START_DATE is the game's calendar epoch: every state and every corpus place opens on it, so it is a scenario default rather than one world's instance. LEXINGTON_DEMO_CONTEXT is the Lexington scenario's own context, used as the lexington-fayette place's context — an explicit scenario, which is what it is for. The module's name reads like a fixture leak and its contents are not one.

src/simulation/demo.ts.reached_by: the src/simulation barrel, and createScenarioWorld from legislation-scenarios
src/simulation/demo.ts.finding: `createScenarioWorld` requires an explicit jurisdiction context and defaults nothing. `createDemoWorld` DOES default its context to Lexington, which would make Kentucky a universal normal start — but ordinary New Game never calls it: its only runtime callers are the Run-A fixture and three src/ui developer proof routes. Pinned behaviourally by src/presentation/dehardwire-place-binding.test.ts, which starts named non-Kentucky lives and asserts neither the jurisdiction nor the clock falls back to Lexington.

src/simulation/portability-fixture.ts.reached_by: the src/simulation barrel's `export *`, and nothing else
src/simulation/portability-fixture.ts.finding: No play-path consumer. It is on the graph because the barrel re-exports it, not because ordinary play uses anything in it.

placeNamingOnThePlayerDossier.was: src/presentation/run-a-projection.ts rendered every birthplace and residence on the player's Quick Dossier through `runAPlaceDisplayName`, the Run-A development fixture's helper, which recognised exactly one place by literal ("Lexington-Fayette, Kentucky" to "Lexington, Kentucky") and passed every other place through as its filing name.
placeNamingOnThePlayerDossier.now: Bound to the place catalog: `lifePlaceByJurisdictionId(id)?.displayName ?? jurisdiction.name`. Every playable place — the four named ones and every row of the national corpus — already carries its resident-facing name beside its formal filing name. A jurisdiction the catalog does not list keeps its own recorded name.
